title: Nine Winters and One Short Arrow
subtitle: 地理地貌 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 地理地貌（人与自然·自然与地理）
meta: 主题语境：地理地貌（人与自然·自然与地理）　|　核心词汇：equator　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 equator 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1889 my great-uncle ① crossed an equator that no sailor on the ship would have marked, and he said the crossing was the whole of the winter. The ② equator, meaning the line itself and not the tropic, ran nine winters and stayed unmarked in the book; an equator, he said, is the only thing on a map that is judged by how long it is left unmarked.

Every ③ equator on that map had the same short arrow beside it, and the ④ equator at the far side, meaning the one they kept for the route and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An equator, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to mark; my great-uncle said the marking is the part that fills nine winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the equator was the whole of the heat, meaning the region and not the line. The ⑥ equator, meaning the region and not any of that, is the only thing in a voyage that everybody hears of and nobody marks; equator, he said, is either something you cross or the only word that means both a line and a region. He said the region is the part they remember.

By 1897 the ⑦ equator had become a line in an atlas, and the atlas had become an argument about the short arrow. The ⑧ equator of the whole thing, my great-uncle wrote in January, was one map and nine winters of marking; equator, he said, is either the one at the far side or the reason you learned to mark. He said the marking was never mentioned.

The ⑨ equator I remember is the one marked in the atlas, which closed in 1901 and is still described as the quietest on the map. An ⑩ equator, my mother said in 1903, is the only one that improves by being marked; every equator, she said, is a region that has agreed to look like a line. She said the region was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 赤道（指地图上每一条旁边的那一条）
B. n. 赤道（指那一条本身，与回归线相对）
C. 固定搭配：cross the equator 穿越赤道
D. n. 赤道（指留给航线的那一条）
E. n. 赤道（抽象总称，指一张地图上的分界之事）
F. n. 赤道（指图册上写到、被标出的那一条）
G. n. 赤道地区（指人人都听说却无人到达的那样地方）
H. n. 赤道地区（抽象总称，指人人都听说却无人到达的那种地带）

answers.why: cross the equator 意为“穿越赤道”，1889 年曾叔父穿越了一条船上没有一位水手肯标出的赤道。
equator 意为“赤道”，指那一条本身而不是回归线，它经过了九个冬天而在簿子上没有记号。
equator 意为“赤道”，指地图上每一条旁边的那一条，每一条旁边都有同一个短短的箭头。
equator 意为“赤道”，指留给航线的那一条，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
equator 意为“赤道地区”，指人人都听说却无人到达的那样地方，叔叔说这片赤道地区就是那份炎热的全部。
equator 意为“赤道地区”，指人人都听说却无人到达的那种地带而不是那一条线，是航程里人人都听说、却无人标出的东西。
equator 意为“赤道”，指图册上写到、被标出的那一条，到 1897 年这一条成了图册里的一行。
equator 意为“赤道”，曾叔父一月写道，整件事的分界之事是一张地图和九个冬天的标出。
equator 意为“赤道”，我记得的是图册上标出的那一条，1901 年结束了，至今仍被说成地图上最安静的一条。
equator 为抽象总称，母亲 1903 年说，一条赤道是唯一会因为被好好标出而变得更好的东西。
